title: ROC (Taiwan) announces closure of mission in Papua New Guinea, comprehensive adjustment of bilateral cooperation, and reallocation of resources to deepen partnerships with diplomatic allies and like-minded countries
text:
The government of Papua New Guinea (PNG) recently renewed its unilateral demands for personnel of the Taipei Economic Office in Port Moresby to leave the country within a specified timeframe and for the mission to be shut down. In consideration of national dignity, diplomatic autonomy, and overall national interests, and following a comprehensive assessment, the ROC (Taiwan) government has made the decision to close the office, withdraw all stationed personnel, and conduct a full review and adjustment of bilateral ties.

The government must appropriately allocate diplomatic resources in accordance with foreign policy considerations and tangible interests. It has therefore taken the initiative to opt for this diplomatic course of action and initiate the aforementioned changes. Moving forward, resources will be redirected to Taiwan’s diplomatic allies and other regions with potential for cooperation and long-term engagement. The government will continue to deepen substantive partnerships with other countries and further expand Taiwan’s international space.

In the spirit of fostering mutual benefit and providing development assistance, Taiwan has consistently given Papua New Guinea concrete support over the years in such areas as the economy, agriculture, health care, and talent development. This has significantly contributed to public well-being and the national development of Papua New Guinea.

Regrettably, the foundation of mutual trust, established through long-term bilateral collaboration, has been seriously undermined by the recent actions of the government of Papua New Guinea. The situation also reflects China’s continued use of political pressure and economic influence to interfere in the diplomatic decisions of other nations and suppress Taiwan’s international participation. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) emphasizes that all nations have the right to independently decide how they engage and cooperate with Taiwan, free from third-party political coercion and manipulation.

Given the damage that has been done to the mutual trust that underpins bilateral cooperation, the government of Taiwan has decided to immediately withdraw all stationed personnel, suspend mission operations, and terminate all technical cooperation and aid programs in Papua New Guinea. These include services provided by the Taiwan Technical and Medical Missions and other related scholarship and talent development initiatives. MOFA will appropriately handle follow-up matters concerning existing partnership programs while ensuring the safety and rights of personnel involved. The decision demonstrates Taiwan’s determination to defend its diplomatic autonomy and overall national interests.

Regarding energy and trade cooperation, Taiwan has ceased spot market purchases of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Papua New Guinea. The projected spot volume procurement for the first half of 2026 was approximately 500,000 tons. No new spot contracts will be signed with Papua New Guinea. Taiwan has long been a key market for Papua New Guinea’snatural gas, accounting for roughly one-third of total LNG exports. The change will inevitably have a substantial impact on Papua New Guinea’s natural gas exports and foreign exchange earnings.

Meanwhile, Taiwan has already completed an assessment of domestic natural gas supply and demand, adjusted procurement allocations, and identified alternative sources. These measures ensure that energy supplies will remain stable and sufficient and will not be affected by the suspension of spot LNG purchases from Papua New Guinea or the recalibration of bilateral relations. This fully demonstrates Taiwan’s ability to diversify energy supplies, autonomouslymake necessary adjustments, and safeguard national energy security and overall interests.

MOFA reiterates that the ROC (Taiwan) is a sovereign and independent country; neither it nor the People’s Republic of China is subordinate to the other. The people of Taiwan have the right to determine their country’s future and participate in the international community on an equal footing.

China has long employed political coercion, economic enticement, and diplomatic suppression in an attempt to force other countries to accept its unilateral political claims and limit Taiwan’s role on the world stage. The Papua New Guinea government’s decision once again highlights China’s use of political and economic tactics to interfere in the sovereign diplomatic choices of other nations. China’s actions undermine international trust and damage the principle of parity.

MOFA calls on the international community to pay heed to China’s continued expansion of political influence and suppression of Taiwan’s international participation. MOFA urges countries worldwide to jointly defend the rules-based international order, common universal democratic values, and the sovereign right of all nations to determine their own foreign policies. Taiwan will not back down in the face of Chinese suppression, nor will it accept efforts by any country to use political pressure to deny its sovereign status and right to participate internationally. Moreover, Taiwan will not squander precious diplomatic resources on relationships that lack mutual trust and a proper basis for cooperation.

Adhering to the principles of pragmatism, reciprocity, and mutual benefit, Taiwan will continue to deepen partnerships with its diplomatic allies and actively expand exchanges with like-minded countries and other regions that show potential for collaboration. To further enhance Taiwan’s global visibility and substantive international contributions, Taiwan will channel diplomatic resources into endeavors that deliver concrete results and align with overall national interests. (E)
